alignments.note: Explanatory conjunction rendered by the verse-initial *For*.

Adverbial accusative plural of πολύς. The supplied *in* realizes the case and rides with the word under rules 7 and 21; *things* is the generic completion of a substantival adjective, so rule 17 heads the unit on *many* and not on *things* or on the preposition.
Inflected verb takes its English subject pronoun as a rule 7/9 helper; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb *stumble* rather than on *we*. Discontinuous under rule 15, *all* intervening.
ἅπαντες rendered by the appositional quantifier *all*.
Ordinary conditional particle aligned to *If* under rule 40.
Indefinite pronoun rendered by a bare *any*. Rule 39's `εἴ τις` → *whoso* is not in question: the ASV writes two English words here, so rule 2 splits the pair.
Finite verb rendered by *stumbleth*; the negative and the prepositional phrase stand as their own units.
Ordinary negative aligned to *not*. Rules 41 and 59 are not in question: no negative indefinite follows.
Preposition governing the prepositional phrase realizes *in* under rule 36, not the verb.
Anarthrous noun rendered by a bare *word*; no determiner is supplied, so nothing else rides with it.

Substantival demonstrative subject of a verbless clause. Rule 68 puts a substantival demonstrative on rule 53's pronoun side, so it takes the supplied copula itself, and rule 63's noun-phrase-predicate case agrees, the predicate *a perfect man* spelling its own determiner, adjective and noun out and leaving nothing inside it for the copula. The supplied nominal *same* is the demonstrative's own English expression under rule 17, which also heads the unit there rather than on *the* or on *is*. The Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied *the* is a rule 51/7 helper on the demonstrative and rule 49 is not in question.
Attributive adjective rendered by a bare *perfect*; the supplied determiner goes to the noun under rule 58.

Both adjective and noun are anarthrous and the ASV supplies *a* for the phrase, so rule 58 gives the determiner to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15. Rule 51's anarthrous clause makes *a* an ordinary rule 7 helper here, no article competing for it.
Complementary infinitive; no conjunction governs the clause, so the infinitival *to* is rule 7's ordinary helper on its own verb rather than rule 40's clause-introducer. Headed on the lexical verb.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19; the attributive adjective takes a bare *whole* under rule 58's closing clause.
ὅλον rendered by *whole*, the article beside it having already taken the determiner.
Head noun rendered by a bare *body*.

Intensifying καί decided on the English alone under rule 65: the ASV writes *also* for it, clause-finally, so it is its own aligned unit. Rule 15 permits the displacement to the end of the clause. The competing reading would leave it unrepresented and read *also* as a free adverb, but rule 65 gives an intensifying καί the word the ASV writes.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged: the accepted alignment survives the audit on every unit. Partition verified — all nineteen s-IDs and all twenty-six t-IDs occur exactly once, every head is a member of its own array, and no unit is source-only or target-only.

s011 οὗτος carries *the same is*. Rule 68 names a substantival demonstrative subject as taking the supplied copula, and rule 63's exception for a noun-phrase predicate points the same way, the predicate *a perfect man* having spelled out an adjective and a noun that already answer to s012 and s013. The two paths agree, so the copula is not the predicate's here. Note extended to say why the supplied *the* rides with the demonstrative: the Greek is anarthrous, so rule 51's anarthrous clause makes it a rule 7 helper and no article competes.

s001's *in many things* keeps the supplied case preposition and the generic noun on the one adverbial accusative, headed on *many* per rule 17's *all things* → *All*. Splitting *in* off would leave nothing for it to answer to, no Greek preposition being expressed, and heading on *things* is what rule 17 forbids.

s012/s013 and s017/s018 are the same phrase shape decided two ways, correctly: *a perfect man* is wholly anarthrous so rule 58 gives the supplied *a* to the noun and leaves *perfect* bare, while *the whole body* has an expressed τό so rule 58's closing clause gives *the* to the article and leaves *whole* bare. Both adjectives end up bare for different reasons, which is the intended reading and not an inconsistency.
s006 τις → a bare *any*: rule 39's `εἴ τις` → *whoso* precedent does not carry, since it wants a single English word and the ASV wrote two. Note amended to record that ruling-out.
s009 οὐ is an ordinary negative on *not*; rules 41 and 59 need no argument beyond the absence of any negative indefinite in the clause, so a reference comparison should show no disagreement here.

s016 καί → *also* remains the only unit where a materially different reading is defensible (unrepresented, with *also* read as a free English adverb). Rule 65's English-side test decides it and the unit's note names the competing reading, as rule 16 requires.
